newsitem.title: INDIA: India economic revival seen in end 97 - First Boston.
newsitem.headline: India economic revival seen in end 97 - First Boston.

text.p: India's slackening industrial growth is likely to revive in the final quarter of 1997, Credit Suisse First Boston said on Tuesday.

"What we forecast is an economic recovery more towards the fourth quarter of this year," K.R. Bharat, managing director at C.S. First Boston India Ltd, told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
"We have seen very little evidence so far that there is a recovery in sight," Bharat added. "The first positive factor came a couple of days ago when some of the trade figures were released."

"June exports actually were up 2.5 percentage points and non-oil imports was up 8.2 percentage which is really encouraging because that's the first time we have got any evidence that economic activity might be picking up."
India's Commerce Ministry reported last week that exports grew by 2.53 percent to $2.66 billion from $2.59 billion a year earlier.
Exports fell by 0.95 percent to $8.13 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) from $8.21 billion a year ago, the government said.
On Monday, Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah said the rupee's recent appreciation against the dollar had affected the country's exports "to some extent."
Ramaiah made the remarks soon after an address to a business seminar in the capital, in reply to queries by reporters.
"Of course to some extent," he said. "Also because neighbouring coutnries like Pakistan and others have devalued. So competition is increasing."
Ramaiah predicted that the rate of export growth in 1997/98 would be higher than in 1996/97, when foreign sales rose 4.01 percent to $33.1 billion.
